messages:
leah: Quick design review: I prototyped a side-by-side weight compare for two scorecard versions (current vs proposed). On narrow widths it collapses awkwardly and keyboard users can't tell which panel is focused. Screenshot: https://img.redwood.test/compare-2240.png

maya: nice! major thing: we need clear focus rings and an announced label when switching panels. Maybe a segmented toggle `Current | Proposed` with aria-pressed states instead of relying on click target only.

leah: I like the segmented toggle approach. Also thinking to surface a short summary above each panel: "Impact: +2.3% overall" so screen readers get context immediately.

samir: implementation note: keep DOM order stable (current then proposed), but allow keyboard to move focus into either panel via the segmented control. Use `aria-live="polite"` to announce the impact summary on change.

nina: copy nit: for save flow we used 'Apply weights to historical runs' which scared folks. Suggest 'Apply weights to historical reports (versioned)' to make versioning explicit. Short variant for button: 'Apply to history (versioned)'.

rong: accessibility nit: when applying to history, we must disclose how many runs are affected. If calculation is async, show a modal with spinner and message: "Computing affected runs..." then update with counts and require an explicit confirm. Screen reader announce: 'Impact computation complete: X runs affected'.

leah: good call. UX variant: immediate small preview + CTA 'Compute impact' (async) vs auto-compute. Which to prefer? Auto-compute is noisy; prefer explicit `Compute impact` button.

maya: agree. button labeling: keep verbs clear. `Compute impact` and then `Apply weights` after counts visible. Also reveal a checkbox `Only apply to passing runs` when mix exists.

samir: dev note: ensure `Compute impact` is cancellable and that progress is announced. When complete, focus should move to the results summary and `Apply weights` button. Return focus to segmented toggle if user cancels.

nina: microcopy for post-compute modal: title `Impact summary` body `Applying this weight set will update X historical reports (Y have failing tests). These changes are versioned and logged.` primary `Apply weights` secondary `Cancel` and tertiary `Save as draft` maybe. Thoughts?

rong: prefer including `Save as draft` (less destructive). Also require an explicit justification textarea if Y>0 and mark it required with min 30 chars. Textarea should support Ctrl+Enter to submit and Enter to insert newline. Helper text: 'Explain why failing runs should be updated (min 30 chars)'.

designbot: Accessibility check: contrast for the proposed panel header on pale bg is 3.4:1 (fails). Recommend darker header token or 1px divider. Also ensure segmented control meets 3:1 contrast for active vs inactive states.

leah: will push header to `neutral-800` and update segmented active color. Also I'll add an aria-describedby that links to the 'versioned' explanation paragraph.

maya: undo flow: after apply show toast 'Weights applied  version v12 created (undo)'. Undo should be keyboard accessible and open a revert modal showing affected runs with option to rollback. Undo window default 5 minutes.

samir: backend will produce parent audit id; include it in toast like 'audit a789'. When Undo clicked, call revert endpoint referencing parent id. We'll gate rollback behind same auth checks.

nina: final tiny copy tweak: Save as draft -> tooltip 'Save as draft: store changes without affecting history' and make sure keyboard users can access tooltip via focus.

leah: awesome. I'll update the figma frames: segmented toggle, compute impact flow, impact modal with counts+justification, save draft option, and stronger contrast tokens. Pushing now 4dd. Review before tomorrow's sync and drop any wording changes here by 11am.
